text:
American farmers did not lobby for daylight saving time: they led the fight that repealed national daylight saving in 1919, over Wilson's veto.

It began as a 1916 German wartime fuel measure. US clocks fell back an hour this morning.

Keep the clock change, or scrap it?

text:
In 1774, three hundred metres of a Paris road dropped into the quarry tunnels beneath it.

Twelve years later a disused quarry was consecrated as an ossuary, and carts arrived after dark, loaded with the dead. It is All Souls' Day.

Would you go down there?

In a Cambridge wind-tunnel film, air over a wing reaches the back edge before air under it.

NASA calls the school story that the two meet there "the most popular incorrect theory of lift". Wings stay up by turning air downward.

Which version were you taught?

text:
The 2010 study said to prove the chicken came first was a computer simulation of calcite crystals forming. It dated nothing and examined no fossils.

The egg came first, by hundreds of millions of years.

Which side were you on?

Nobody designed QWERTY to slow typists down.

It began in 1868 as a piano-style alphabetical keyboard. A telegraph school advertised the machine as producing letters "faster than the most rapid penman".

Who first told you that one?

A fly that walks across your plate has already sampled it before its mouthparts arrive.

Much of its sense of taste and all of its grip live in its feet. Flies rub their legs together to clean them.

Four pet cats have been filmed sitting inside a square that was not there: an illusion made of four Pac-Man shapes taped to the floor, cut-out corners facing inward.

They sat in it seven times. A real square outline drew cats eight times.

Has your cat ever done this?

Nearly every golden hamster in a cage descends from a brother and sister mated in Jerusalem in 1930.

They came from a litter dug out of a wheat field near Aleppo, Syria. Wild ones are Endangered, and trapped and poisoned as crop pests.

Did you have a hamster growing up?

In its 2000 edition, the US government's own style manual called noon 12 a.m. and midnight 12 p.m. Its 2008 edition reversed both.

NIST says 12 a.m. and 12 p.m. "are ambiguous and should not be used."

What do you write for noon?

second.text: Santa Claus Village began as a cabin for Eleanor Roosevelt.

text:
More red light than blue comes back from synthetic skin above an artificial vein, a 2026 optics study found.

The vein reads blue only because the skin beside it returns even more red. Human blood is red at every oxygen level.

Were you taught the blue blood version?

second.text: The longest word in English dictionaries reached them by way of a puzzlers' meeting.

text:
For seven years, the federal Veterans Day fell in October.

The first "was observed with much confusion" on October 25, 1971, and it went back to November 11 in 1978. Today is Veterans Day.

second.text: The Titanic is sometimes credited with the first SOS, but the call was on the air nearly three years earlier.

text:
In 1962, Popular Mechanics called Einstein a man "who never took an intelligence test" and, in the same parenthesis, gave his estimated IQ as 207.

There is no record that he ever took one. The famous 160 has no test behind it either.

Which number had you heard?
thread:
In 1962, Popular Mechanics called Einstein a man "who never took an intelligence test" and, in the same parenthesis, gave his estimated IQ as 207.

There is no record that he ever took one. The famous 160 has no test behind it either.

Which number had you heard?

The figure usually quoted is 160. In 2022 The Independent, setting a schoolboy beside Stephen Hawking, wrote that Einstein "is said to have had an IQ of around 160, although it is unclear whether either man did a test."
There is no record that Einstein ever took an intelligence test. The Army Alpha of 1917, which psychologist Russell Warne calls the first successful one for adults, came when Einstein was 38.

In 1954 a father recalled being told his son's IQ was 185, asking, "Genius is about 160, isn't it?" and hearing, "Albert Einstein's is probably a little higher." Whether that meant above 160 or 185 is unclear.
Nobody knows Einstein's IQ. In 2023 Warne concluded that "any currently existing claims of an IQ score for Albert Einstein are not credible."

second.text: The crack that brought down Comet G-ALYP probably began near the rear ADF window, one of two radio aerial windows in the cabin roof.

text:
The real Illuminati used an owl and was outlawed in Bavaria by 1785.

The dollar's eye and pyramid come from the Great Seal of 1782, whose official description sets no number of steps: the 13 are a tradition. It is Friday the 13th.

Got a dollar bill handy? Count the steps.

second.text: The sled reindeer of Scandinavia and Finland were traditionally castrated bulls, and unlike full males they kept their antlers through the winter.

text:
A spotted hyena's giggle often comes from one kept off a kill by higher-ranking clanmates.

Researchers read the call as submission and frustration, not amusement. Its pitch can even carry clues to the caller's age.

A capital M set in 12-point type is not 12 points of anything.

The em dash was cast one em wide, and an em is a unit equal to the type size. The M that lent the unit its name does not fill the em square.

Do you still use em dashes?

Alexander Bain, a Scottish clockmaker, patented a fax machine in 1843.

Paris was faxing Lyon in 1865, 11 years before Bell patented the telephone. Fax machines filled offices in the 1980s.

When did you last send a fax?

text:
A Moon that had stopped rotating would show Earth every side of itself once a month.

The real one rotates once on its axis in exactly the time it takes to orbit Earth, roughly 27.3 days, so the same hemisphere stays pointed at Earth.

Did you think it didn't spin?

slides.head: Two mistakes
slides.body: The hidden hemisphere is still routinely called the dark side. A second mistake travels with the nickname: the idea that the Moon does not spin at all.

slides.head: Spin and orbit match
slides.body: The Moon rotates once on its axis in exactly the time it takes to orbit Earth, roughly 27.3 days. Astronomers call this tidal locking.

slides.head: Not dark, just far
slides.body: The far side gets as much sunlight as the near side. Dark meant unknown, not unlit. Luna 3 first photographed it on 7 October 1959.

slides.head: The answer
slides.body: We see one side because the Moon spins once per orbit, so the same hemisphere stays pointed at Earth. A wobble called libration shows us about 59% of the surface over time.

second.text: Niels Bohr showed in his doctoral dissertation of 1911 that classical physics cannot account for magnetism in materials.

text:
More than 99% of Earth's gold lies in the core, under about 3,000 km of solid rock.

Every gold ring, coin and circuit board ever made came out of the sliver outside it. Most of that gold is thought to have arrived later, on meteorites.
thread:
More than 99% of Earth's gold lies in the core, under about 3,000 km of solid rock.

Every gold ring, coin and circuit board ever made came out of the sliver outside it. Most of that gold is thought to have arrived later, on meteorites.
Gold is formed in space, not in the ground. Fusion in stars stops at iron, because "iron releases no energy when fused."
Iron has 26 protons and gold has 79. Gold forms mostly when rare cataclysms like neutron-star collisions flood nuclei with neutrons faster than they can decay.
In 2017 astronomers caught two neutron stars colliding in a galaxy about 130 million light years away. From the glow, researchers estimated a yield of around 200 Earth masses of gold.
Gold is made in space, mostly in rare blasts like neutron-star collisions. The gold we mine is thought to have come later on meteorites, gathered into quartz veins and river gravels.

second.text: The quotations for Irish twins in Green's Dictionary of Slang begin with a newspaper and a baby, in the Louisville Daily Courier of June 4, 1852.

text:
The poop deck is named for the poop, an old word for a ship's stern recorded in English by 1489, two centuries before poop had any bodily sense.

The crew's toilets were at the bow. It is World Toilet Day.

second.text: The first genetically engineered product the Food and Drug Administration approved for use in food was an enzyme for making cheese.

text:
Bluetooth was meant to be called PAN, the winner of a 4-1 vote.

PAN could not be trademarked, and the backup, RadioWire, had not been searched in time. The stand-in codename, named after a 10th-century Danish king, stuck.

Would PAN have caught on?

second.text: In a test reported in 1951, six cats detected light almost six times dimmer, on average, than two people could.

text:
For 52 and a half years, a US federal rule said a television's size, unless the seller said otherwise, meant the width of its picture.

The diagonal, the figure every set is sold by, needed a label until 2019. It is World Television Day.

Oregon's famous exploding whale was blown up on purpose, with half a ton of dynamite, by the state Highway Division in 1970.

One chunk flattened a parked car a quarter-mile away. "It went just exactly right," the engineer said.

text:
Nobody can write out Graham's number in ordinary digits, but its final digits are known: they end in 4195387.

It once held the record for the biggest number in a mathematical proof. It is Fibonacci Day, 11/23.

What's the biggest number you can name?

second.text: The word barnacle first named a bird, the barnacle goose, and is not recorded for the animal itself until the 1580s.

text:
The two accounts of the 1620 Plymouth landing written by people who were there mention no rock.

Plymouth Rock was pointed out about 1741 by a church elder in his nineties, citing his father, who arrived in 1623. It is Thanksgiving week.

Have you seen Plymouth Rock?

second.text: Terman's 1916 handbook counted any person over 16, however old, as just 16 years old for purposes of calculating I Q.

text:
Rafter, the trivia answer for a group of turkeys, sounds medieval but has not been traced in print before 1908.

Gang was in print by 1709, and flock, the usual word, by 1657. Thanksgiving is tomorrow.

What would you call a group of turkeys?

second.text: From Dunder and Blixem to Donner and Blitzen, the last two of Santa's reindeer have meant thunder and lightning.

text:
Gram for gram, chicken breast has about as much tryptophan as turkey breast, and parmesan has more.

If tryptophan were the reason turkey makes people sleepy, chicken would do the job just as well. Happy Thanksgiving.

second.text: Only two countries produced more rapeseed oil than Germany in 2023: China, and Canada, where a new rapeseed was bred and renamed canola.

text:
In 1890, fourteen resellers in Brest protested in elegant calligraphy when a paper called the town's fair a flea market.

The name jeered at secondhand rags believed to carry fleas, and it stuck anyway. It is Black Friday.

Best thing you ever found at a flea market?

second.text: Shulgi, king of the Sumerian city of Ur, claimed in a hymn to have run from Nippur to Ur and back in one day.

text:
Cornell's cat behavior expert rejects the snake theory behind the cucumber videos.

Cats have no natural fear of snakes, she said, and many hunt them. In an Australian study, six of 358 feral and stray cats had eaten venomous snakes.

The X in Xmas is not the English letter X but the Greek letter chi, the first letter of Christos.

English scribes used it as shorthand for Christ by the 11th century, long before advertising. Advent starts today.

The original spec says "the state object is called a cookie, for no compelling reason." It is Cyber Monday.
